text:
Aisha: Heads-up  we keep getting requests from Support asking why auth failures don't include org/project so they can triage faster. Is anyone comfortable returning org/proj IDs in the API error payload?

Tom: returning full IDs in responses is handy for support but is an exposure risk. Where would those responses appear? Client logs, Sentry, browser console?

Aisha: mostly server->client responses that could bubble into customer logs or Sentry. Example proposed payload from Support: 
```json
{
  "error": "permission_denied",
  "resource": "project:proj_abc123",
  "needs": "inference.invoker"
}
```

Carlos: strong -1. Compliance showed us incidents where leaked identifiers hurt customers. Also some customers explicitly forbid logging of identifiers from their side.

Maya: alternative: return an opaque reference token and keep a server-side mapping. Clients get `X-Authz-Ref: authz_01FJ...` or an `authz_ref` field. Support can look it up in Console only if authorized.

Tom: implementation sketch: generate short opaque id, store mapping in internal table with fields: org_id, project_id, request_id, token_fingerprint, created_at, ttl. Return minimal error + authz_ref header. Example response: 
```json
{
  "error": "permission_denied",
  "authz_ref": "authz_rk1x9"
}
```
We expose a Console resolver that resolves `authz_rk1x9` for staff with `support:resolve_auth_ref` permission.

Aisha: Nice. Questions: 1) retention TTL? 2) opt-in per org? 3) how do we ensure this data doesn't leak into customer-side logs (we still return something)?

Carlos: default TTL 30d. For free orgs reduce to 7d. Make the mapping creation controlled by an org setting: `authz_ref_enabled` (enterprise default ON). That respects customers that disallow any identifiers being stored.

Maya: UX notes: Console resolver should show redacted view for non-privileged folks and full details only when RBAC allows. Also surface `expires_at` and a small activity timeline showing when the ref was resolved. Audit log each resolution with actor.

Tom: security notes: generate refs with HMAC using rotating secret, avoid sequential ids. Make creation constant-time to avoid timing leaks. Also ratelimit mapping creations per token to avoid storage amplification attacks.

Aisha: what about Sentry / customer-side tooling capturing the response including `authz_ref`? Does that matter?

Carlos: `authz_ref` itself is safe to leak; it maps to internal context only. But if org toggles OFF, we must omit the field entirely so nothing is client-visible. Also we should redact it from any error message templates before sending to external logging services (we control SDKs in many customers).

Maya: ops: include `token_fingerprint` and `request_hash` in mapping so we can correlate even if customers try to claim a request. Also show TTL countdown in Console and a single-click copy of the ref for support.

Tom: will do a spike: add `X-Authz-Ref` header + POST to internal mapping service. Ill add a feature flag guarded behind `authz_ref_spike`.

auth-bot: deploy-bot: CI started for branch tom/authz-ref-spike :gear: build queued

Carlos: compliance follow-up  Ill check with Legal about storing minimal metadata vs identifiers. If Legal objects, we can fallback to ephemeral in-memory mapping only preserved for 24h.

Aisha: action items: 
- Tom: prototype header + mapping + console resolver spike.
- Carlos: compliance + legal check on retention and default opt-in.
- Maya: console mock for resolver + RBAC + audit UX.

Tom: Ill post the spike PR link when ready. Keep the feature flagged. Also will add unit tests that verify mapping TTL and redact behavior when org toggle is off.

Aisha: Thanks. If everyone agrees, we'll proceed with spike and reconvene next week. :thumbsup:
